name: LMV358IDR
title: LMV321, LMV358 and LMV324: single, dual and quad 2.7 V to 5.5 V op amps with rail-to-rail output
summary: Low-voltage general-purpose op amps in one, two and four channels (LMV321, LMV358, LMV324) for 2.7 V to 5.5 V supplies. The output swings close to both rails, the input common-mode range reaches slightly below ground, and the dual draws 210 µA typical for both amplifiers at 5 V, with 1 MHz of unity-gain bandwidth. All grades run from -40 °C to 125 °C. LMV358IDR is the I-grade dual in an 8-pin SOIC on a 2500-piece reel.

circuits.title: Single-ended input to differential output conversion
circuits.description: One LMV358 turns a single-ended 0.5 V to 2 V input into a ±1.5 V differential output from one 2.7 V supply. Amplifier 1 is a unity-gain follower, so VOUT+ copies VIN. Amplifier 2 inverts VOUT+ through R1 and R2 and adds half of the 2.5 V reference, divided by R3 and R4, scaled by its noninverting gain; with all four resistors equal VOUT– equals VREF minus VIN. VDIFF is taken between the two outputs, and the common-mode level sits at VREF/2.

parts.note: amplifier 1 is the buffer, amplifier 2 the inverting stage
matched to R2, R3 and R4; within 2 %

notes: The resistor value, 36 kΩ with a measured spread inside 2 %, is the one this design was built with. Values of 6 kΩ or less keep the resistor noise below the amplifier noise when noise matters.
Because the LMV358 has a 1 MHz bandwidth, the circuit handles signals below 1 MHz.
Swept from 0 V to 2.5 V the output stays linear only between 0.5 V and 2 V of input.

circuits.title: Noninverting amplifier (layout example)
circuits.description: A noninverting stage: the input reaches the noninverting input through RIN, and the gain is set by RF from the output to the inverting input and RG from the inverting input to ground. RF and RG sit close to the inverting input to keep stray capacitance low. Amplifier 2 of the dual is unused.

parts.note: low-ESR ceramic, at the VCC+ pin

notes: For split supplies the GND pin becomes VS– and takes its own 0.1 µF bypass capacitor to ground.

equations.name: Inverting output (Equation 2)
equations.expr: VOUT– = VREF × (R4 / (R3 + R4)) × (1 + R2 / R1) – VIN × R2 / R1

where.R1: input resistor of the inverting stage
where.R3: upper resistor of the reference divider
where.R4: lower resistor of the reference divider

equations.name: Differential output (Equation 3)
equations.expr: VDIFF = VOUT+ – VOUT– = VIN × (1 + R2 / R1) – VREF × (R4 / (R3 + R4)) × (1 + R2 / R1)

equations.name: Outputs with R1 = R2 and R3 = R4 (Equations 4 and 5)
Differential output with R1 = R2 and R3 = R4 (Equation 6)
equations.note: The largest input equals VREF, each output reaches at most VREF, and the differential range is 2 × VREF.

where.Vcm: common-mode voltage of the two outputs

operation.text: LMV321, LMV358 and LMV324 hold one, two and four amplifiers. They run from 2.7 V to 5.5 V, have rail-to-rail outputs, accept common-mode inputs down to ground, and offer a slew rate of 1 V/µs with a unity-gain bandwidth of 1 MHz. Their specifications meet or beat those of the LM358 and LM324, which need 5 V to 30 V. LMV321A, LMV358A and LMV324A are upgraded versions.
The I and Q temperature grades both cover -40 °C to 125 °C free air.

The amplifiers are fully specified at 2.7 V and 5 V, with many limits holding over -40 °C to 125 °C; the typical curves show what shifts strongly with supply or temperature. A supply above 5.5 V can destroy the part. The parts work from a single supply or from split supplies, and are on whenever the supply is present.
Unity-gain bandwidth, the highest frequency a unity-gain stage passes without serious distortion, is 1 MHz. Slew rate, the fastest the output can move after an input change, is 1 V/µs.
One amplifier can be shorted to ground indefinitely at 25 °C or below with VCC up to 5.5 V. A short from an output to VCC can heat the part until it fails.
The LMV321 comes in the SC-70 (DCK) package, about half the size of SOT-23 (DBV), which saves board area and lets the amplifier sit nearer the signal source, where it picks up less noise.

Put a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor close to the supply pins to keep noise from a noisy or high-impedance supply out of the amplifier. On split supplies each supply pin takes a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor to ground, as near the part as possible; on a single supply one such capacitor on V+ is enough.

Keep analog and digital grounds apart and watch where ground current flows; a ground plane on an inner layer spreads heat and lowers EMI pickup. Route input traces short and well away from supply and output traces, and if a sensitive trace must cross a noisy one, cross at right angles. Place the external parts close to the amplifier, with RF and RG next to the inverting input. Critical traces can be ringed with a guard trace held at low impedance, which cuts leakage from neighbouring traces at other potentials.

operation.topic: Typical application: amplifier and parts choice
operation.text: In the single-ended to differential converter DC linearity is limited by how far the inputs and the output can go toward the rails, so a part whose input and output both reach the rails suits it best. The transfer function depends directly on R1 to R4, so tight-tolerance resistors keep the error down.
